mainEntity.name: How much does a MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace a MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 engine varies by generation and condition. Used engines typically range from £1,200 to £2,200, while reconditioned units cost between £2,200 and £3,500. A fully rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty generally ranges from £3,000 to £4,800, excluding labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling or metallic ticking noise from the engine bay, particularly during a cold start. Other symptoms include the check engine light illuminating, rough idling, loss of power, or a "death rattle" that worsens with engine speed.

mainEntity.name: Does the ALL4 all-wheel-drive system affect engine replacement cost or time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the ALL4 system adds a small amount of complexity to the replacement process. Removing and reinstalling the rear driveshaft and transfer case typically adds around 1 hour to the specialist labour time compared to a front-wheel-drive Cooper S. However, the core engine supply costs remain identical.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a 2010-2016 MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's overall condition and current market value, which typically ranges from £3,000 to £7,000 for this era. If the rest of the car is in excellent condition with low mileage, a reconditioned engine can extend its life reliably.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the N18 and B48 engines in the MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N18 (2010-2016) is a 1.6L turbocharged 4-cylinder engine producing 184 hp, known for its punchy delivery but also its timing chain vulnerabilities. The B48 (2017-2023) is a 2.0L turbocharged 4-cylinder engine producing 192 hp. The B48 features a rear-mounted timing chain, improved thermal management, and significantly better long-term reliability.

commonProblems.h3: The MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 is a capable performance SUV, but the N18B16A engine dominates replacement demand due to well-documented timing chain vulnerabilities. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 N18B16A Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 (N18B16A, 2010-2016)
problems.rootCause: The original timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure over time, allowing the chain to stretch and slap against the plastic guides. This creates a rattling noise on cold starts and can eventually lead to catastrophic internal engine damage if the chain jumps.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the chain, tensioner, and guides before catastrophic failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Good if caught early (no engine knock), extends life by 50k+ miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The only viable option once the chain has jumped or caused internal damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical R60 MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 (2010-2016) is currently valued between £3,000 and £7,000 depending on condition and mileage [THIRD-PARTY]. An F60 model (2017-2023) typically ranges from £10,000 to £20,000+ [THIRD-PARTY]. If your R60 vehicle is worth under £5,000, a full rebuilt engine may approach the car's total value, making a quality used engine or preventative repair the more financially sensible route. For F60 models, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is strongly justified to protect the vehicle's significant residual value.
problems.recommendation: For N18-equipped MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 models, a preventative timing chain replacement is critical if it has not been done already. If catastrophic failure has already occurred, a full replacement with a rebuilt unit featuring upgraded components is the only reliable long-term solution.

problems.group: Cooling System Leaks & Thermostat Housing Failure
problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks & Thermostat Housing Failure - Why the MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 Overheats
problems.affectedModels: MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 (N18B16A, B48A20A, 2010-2023)
problems.rootCause: The plastic composite thermostat housing and water pump assemblies are prone to cracking under repeated heat cycles, leading to slow coolant loss, overheating warnings, and potential head gasket failure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the thermostat housing, water pump, and flushing the cooling system.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective for resolving leaks if the engine block is otherwise healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt unit with updated cooling components and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if severe overheating has caused secondary internal damage or warped the cylinder head.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, evaluate the £3,000-£20,000+ value band based on your MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4's year. For a lower-value R60 model, spending £4,000+ on a rebuilt engine is rarely economical unless the car has exceptional low-mileage value.
problems.recommendation: Regular coolant flushes and immediate attention to minor leaks can prevent catastrophic overheating. If the MINI Countryman Cooper S / Cooper S ALL4 engine has already warped the cylinder head due to overheating, a full replacement with a rebuilt unit is the most cost-effective and reliable path forward.
